title: Drift a sprung splice plate into line, bolt it, then swap the drift for the last bolt
instruction: Bolt the blue splice plate to the grey flange through both holes. Use the drift pin, then stand it back in its holder.
context: Structural iron and steel workers line up connection holes with a drift pin, bolt the free holes, then knock out the drifts and bolt those holes too (O*NET 47-2221.00 Structural Iron and Steel Workers; 49-9044.00 Millwrights do the same on machine bases). Holes that do not line up by hand are normal in fit-up, and the drift's taper does the moving. Board pin tasks (pin-fit, aligning two pipe flanges and pinning them) seat a pin in holes that are already in line; here the tool must make the line against a spring (a plate pushed over by hand or pried with the drift does not count), and the drift may come out only after another bolt holds it.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); z is height above the table top. Table: oak-coloured top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. Flange: fixed, centred at x 27, y 0: two dark steel legs 12 x 1.5 x 6 cm (y -11.75 and +11.75) under a grey steel plate 12 x 25 x 2 cm (z 6 to 8), with two slotted holes 3.0 (x) by 3.6 (y) cm at y -8 (hole A) and +8 (hole B), open below. Guide: a fixed dark steel bar 2 x 25 x 7 cm stands against the flange's far edge (x 33 to 35). On its top, along y, is a 9 mm miniature ball linear guide (MGN9 size: rail 21 cm long, one 2 x 4 cm block, 1 cm tall together), and at each end a dark steel post 1 x 1 x 2.5 cm (y -12 and +12). Splice plate: blue acetal (POM), 10 x 22 x 1.5 cm (z 8.03 to 9.53), with a 3 x 4 cm lug of the same thickness on its far edge screwed to the guide block; 445 g with the lug (470 g moving with the block). The guide carries it 0.3 mm clear of the flange, free along y only. Springs: two steel extension springs, 75 N/m each, run along y from the two ends of the lug to the two posts, each 9.5 cm long and pulling 3.0 N at rest. Together they give no force at rest and 1.5 N per cm of slide: 2.9 N at 1.9 cm, 5.1 N at 3.4 cm. At rest the lug is at y 0 and the plate sits 2.9 cm toward -y from where its holes would sit over the flange's. Its two slotted holes (3.0 x 3.6 cm) are at y +-7.7 in its own frame, 0.6 cm closer together than the flange's, so at rest a 1.0 cm strip of hole A and a 0.4 cm strip of hole B show through the plate. Travel: stop collars on the rail at 0.3 cm toward -y and 3.4 cm toward +y of rest. Drift pin: orange acetal, one piece, 100 g, hanging by its head: head 4.0 x 2.9 x 4.0 cm, shank 2.0 x 2.9 x 2.0 cm, then a 4.0 cm taper that narrows in y from 2.9 to 0.3 cm (6 cm below the head in all). Bolts: two, yellow acetal, one piece, 75 g each: head 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.0 cm, a grip tab 4.0 (x) x 1.8 (y) x 3.0 cm on top, and a 1.6 x 1.6 cm shank 6 cm long whose last 1 cm is chamfered to 1.3 cm. Holders: three fixed dark steel collars, each 6.5 cm tall with a 3.2 cm square opening and 1 cm walls (5.2 cm square outside); a part hangs by its head on the rim with its tip 0.5 cm above the table, so its top is 10.5 cm up: drift at x 19, y -16.5; one bolt at x 19, y -24.5; the other at x 19, y +17.
scoring: Open both grippers first; timing from video. J: plate slide from rest (ruler). Gap: drift to flange hole A's edge plus drift to the plate hole's far edge (feeler gauge). Lined up: the drift's tip entered hole A with J 0.3 cm or less, then the drift stood in it (tip below the plate, tilt up to 15 degrees) with J 1.4 cm or more and gap 3 mm or less for 1 s. Before that, J over 0.3 cm with gap over 3 mm for 0.25 s (pushed or pried) voids the entry: restart from rest. Bolt home: tip 5 mm or more below the flange, head within 4 mm of the plate top, tilt up to 5 degrees, within 1.2 cm of a hole axis. 0.25: lined up. 0.5: then a bolt went home with the drift in a hole. 0.75: both holes have a bolt home. 1.0: also the drift stands in its holder (head within 1 cm of the rim, tilt up to 10 degrees, centred within 1.5 cm), parts still. Otherwise, or a part off the table: 0.
reset_notes: Let the springs bring the plate back to rest (J 0); a spring scale on each spring should read 3.0 N there. Hang the drift and both bolts by their heads in their holders. Nothing is consumed or bent. In a real trial keep fingers off the plate edges and out of the holes while the plate is under spring load (the simulation cannot score this).
fidelity: Rigid-body approximation: the guide and the two springs are one slide joint (150 N/m, 10 N s/m damping in place of guide drag) and the springs are not drawn; holes are boxes and the taper is two tilted slabs. Parts have friction 1.0 so the grippers hold them; real acetal slides more easily. Bolts are not tightened. The last step is scored with the grippers still closed, so a part more than 1 cm above its seat counts as not placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved arms to the table edges, never touched the drift or bolts); demo: 1.0 (drifted plate into line, bolted both holes, stood drift back in holder)
